text_blocks.snippet: Jupiter is the largest planet in our solar system.

list.snippet: Mass: More than 300 times heavier than Earth and 2.5 times more massive than all other solar system planets combined.
Size: Has an equatorial diameter of about 88,900 miles (143,000 km), which is roughly 11 times wider than Earth.
Volume: Large enough to hold about 1,000 Earths inside.
Rotation: Spins very fast, completing one full rotation (a day) in about 9.9 hours.
Composition: Made mostly of hydrogen and helium, operating as a gas giant with no solid surface.
Learn More: Explore further details and updates from the NASA Jupiter Science page.

perspectives.title: Jupiter didn’t just become the biggest planet, it became the reason Earth even exists.
